subtitle: How a Forest Kingdom Became a Web of Sacred Villages

panels.shot: wide aerial over dense Western Ghats forests broken by neat village clearings
panels.action: Mayurasharma’s Land Grants stands as a dignified royal figure in the foreground, scroll in hand, while below him tax-free agrahara villages glow like small islands of order amid dark forested hills and winding rivers.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Kadambas, Mayurasharma’s sword won a kingdom—but his tax‑free agrahara villages turned it into a quiet machine that still shapes the Kannada land.

i18n.hi: कदंबों के दौर में, मयूरशर्मा की तलवार ने राज्य जीता—but उसके कर‑मुक्त आग्रहारा गाँवों ने उसे एक शांत मशीन बना दिया, जो आज भी कन्नड भूमि गढ़ती है।

panels.shot: close, low-angle on an inscribed stone pillar against sky
panels.action: An imposing stone pillar at Talagunda rises from the earth, its early script lines sharply carved, as Mayurasharma’s Land Grants appears faintly beside it like a thoughtful ghost-figure, hand resting lightly on the inscription.

dialogue.text: On a quiet plain at Talagunda, a stone pillar remembers an agrahara of Brahmins, their books, their fire—an agrahara that, the inscription insists, birthed a dynasty of kings.

i18n.hi: तलागुंडा के सन्नाटे भरे मैदान में, एक पत्थर का स्तंभ याद करता है ब्राह्मणों का एक आग्रहारा—उनकी किताबें, उनकी अग्नि—वही आग्रहारा, जो, शिलालेख कहता है, एक राजवंश को जन्म देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a village school courtyard
panels.action: Young Brahmin boys sit cross‑legged under a shady tree in an early agrahara courtyard at Sthanagundur, reciting from palm‑leaf manuscripts while an elder teacher gestures with a palm leaf, and Mayurasharma’s Land Grants watches from the side, absorbing the scene.

dialogue.text: The Talagunda record speaks of Sthanagundur, an agrahara where Brahmins memorised Vedic verses, taught grammar and ritual, and lived by gifts instead of tax and plough.

i18n.hi: तलागुंडा का लेख स्थलनगर के आग्रहारा की बात करता है—जहाँ ब्राह्मण वेद रटते, व्याकरण और विधि पढ़ाते, और हल‑कर छोड़ दान से जीते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Mayurasharma’s face as he reads
panels.action: Mayurasharma’s Land Grants sits cross‑legged indoors, lit by an oil lamp, reading a palm‑leaf charter, brows furrowed as faint scenes of forest warriors and Gupta‑era courts shimmer in the darkness behind him.

dialogue.text: From such a world, the Talagunda inscription says, came Mayurasharma, a Brahmin student who turned to arms and, in time, carved a kingdom in the forests of Banavasi.

i18n.hi: यहीं से, शिलालेख कहता है, निकला मयूरशर्मा—एक ब्राह्मण छात्र, जिसने हथियार उठाए और समय के साथ बनवासी के जंगलों में एक राज्य तराश दिया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Banavasi landscape with fort and forests
panels.action: A panoramic view of early Banavasi shows a modest fort atop a hill, dense Western Ghats forests spreading beyond, humble hamlets along a river, and Mayurasharma’s Land Grants standing at the edge, surveying land and horizon.

dialogue.text: This was no open plain of endless fields. Banavasi lay in broken hills and forests, scattered settlements, shifting chiefs—the kind of land a conqueror could seize but not easily hold.

i18n.hi: ये अंतहीन खेतों का खुला मैदान नहीं था। बनवासी थी टूटी पहाड़ियों और जंगलों की भूमि—छिटके गाँव, बदलते सरदार—ऐसी धरती, जिसे जीता जा सकता था, पर आसानी से थामा नहीं जा सकता था।

panels.shot: dynamic oblique shot of Mayurasharma amid armed followers
panels.action: Mayurasharma’s Land Grants stands in armour at the head of a small Kadamba warband, spears and banners raised, forest behind them and a dirt track leading towards distant villages, his face determined yet thoughtful.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions remember his victories, his ashvamedha sacrifice, the clash with Pallavas and others. Yet they are quiet about one question: once won, how would this wild country be ordered?

i18n.hi: शिलालेख उसकी जीतें गिनते हैं—अश्वमेध, पल्लवों से टक्कर और औरों से भी—but एक सवाल पर चुप हैं: जीती हुई इस जंगली धरती को अब कैसे सँभाला गया?

panels.shot: close shot of an ashvamedha horse and ritual ground
panels.action: A richly caparisoned horse stands tethered near an ashvamedha altar, priests and attendants moving about the sacred ground, while Mayurasharma’s Land Grants watches from the background, scroll tucked into his waistband instead of a sword.

dialogue.text: Later copper plates will boast that he performed an ashvamedha, the proud horse sacrifice of emperors—a ritual that demanded priests, gifts, and a public claim to supreme sovereignty.

i18n.hi: बाद के ताम्रपत्र शान से कहेंगे कि उसने अश्वमेध किया—सम्राटों की घोड़ा‑यज्ञ—जो मांगता था पुरोहित, दान, और सबके सामने सर्वोच्च सत्ता का दावा।

panels.shot: tight overhead shot of a copper plate set on a wooden desk
panels.action: A copper plate charter lies on a wooden desk, its letters freshly incised and gleaming, while Mayurasharma’s Land Grants presses his seal onto a cord, his other hand pointing to the lines specifying a tax‑free village grant.

dialogue.text: From these plates at Halasi, we hear another boast: that Mayurasharma granted no fewer than 144 brahmadeya villages to Brahmins—villages lifted out of tax and king’s demand.

i18n.hi: हलेसी के इन पट्टों से एक और शेखी सुनाई देती है: मयूरशर्मा ने ब्राह्मणों को पूरे १४४ ब्रह्मदेय गाँव दिए—गाँव, जो कर और राज आदेश से ऊपर उठा दिए गए।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view mapping villages across hills and rivers
panels.action: From above, a stylised map of the western Karnataka hills shows scattered villages connected by faint glowing lines, with Mayurasharma’s Land Grants superimposed, stretching his arm as if laying those lines across the land.

dialogue.text: Not all those 144 places can be traced today, the ground has changed. But the record is clear: the Kadambas turned their forest realm into a network of brahmadeya nodes.

i18n.hi: आज सब १४४ जगहें नहीं मिलतीं, ज़मीन बदल गई। पर दस्तावेज़ साफ कहते हैं: कदंबरों ने अपने वन‑राज्य को ब्रह्मदेय ठिकानों के जाल में बदल दिया।

panels.shot: medium shot inside an agrahara street
panels.action: Inside an agrahara, neat rows of tiled houses line a clean street; Brahmin householders tend small gardens, a ritual fire burns in a courtyard, and Mayurasharma’s Land Grants walks with a local Brahmin elder, gesturing toward the homes.

dialogue.speaker: mayurasharma_s_land_grants
dialogue.text: In this village, your books and rites will guard my frontier better than spears.

i18n.hi: इस गाँव में, तुम्हारी किताबें और विधि मेरी सरहद को भालों से भी बेहतर बचाएँगी।

panels.shot: close-up of hand marking boundaries in the field
panels.action: Mayurasharma’s Land Grants and village elders stand at the edge of a field; one elder plants a boundary stone while another points to a distant tree line, as Mayurasharma marks the line with a staff in the soil.

dialogue.text: The grant meant more than charity. Boundaries were walked, trees and tanks named, fields counted, rights over land and labour redirected from king’s agents to Brahmin donees.

i18n.hi: ये दान सिर्फ दया नहीं था। हदें नापी गईं, पेड़‑तालों के नाम लिखे गए, खेत गिने गए—और जमीन‑मेहनत पर हक राजा के कर्मचारियों से हटकर ब्राह्मण दानियों को दे दिए गए।

panels.shot: split-scene composition of temple and school within same village
panels.action: Within a single panel, one side shows a small stone shrine with priests performing worship, while the other shows a teacher instructing pupils with palm leaves; Mayurasharma’s Land Grants stands between these halves, linking them with an outstretched hand.

dialogue.text: In these brahmadeyas, land revenue fed Vedic teachers, ritual specialists, temple worship, perhaps early record‑keepers—tying sacred learning and administration to the soil itself.

i18n.hi: इन ब्रह्मदेयों में, भूमि का लगान वेदाध्यापकों, विधि‑पुरोहितों, देवपूजा, शायद शुरुआती लेखक‑कर्मियों तक जाता था—पवित्र विद्या और राजकाज को मिट्टी से बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of a mixed village assembly under a tree
panels.action: Under a large tree in an agrahara village, Brahmin elders sit in front while cultivators and artisans stand or sit behind; Mayurasharma’s Land Grants sits slightly apart, listening as one elder speaks with a raised hand.

dialogue.text: Sharma and Chattopadhyaya read such grants as early feudal ties: the king gave land and immunity, Brahmins owed loyalty, ritual honour, and local leadership over tenants and dependants.

i18n.hi: शर्मा और चट्टोपाध्याय ऐसे दान को शुरुआती सामंती गठजोड़ मानते हैं: राजा ने जमीन और छूट दी, ब्राह्मण ने वफादारी, यज्ञ‑सम्मान और किरायेदारों व आश्रितों पर स्थानीय नेतृत्व।

panels.shot: medium shot of Mayurasharma weighing a sword against a copper plate
panels.action: Mayurasharma’s Land Grants stands before a simple balance scale; on one side rests a sword, on the other a stack of copper plates, and he looks at the heavier side where the plates tip the balance.

dialogue.text: Battles won a moment of fear. A copper plate, once issued, could yield quiet obedience year after year, without a single spear raised.

i18n.hi: युद्ध बस एक पल का भय जीतते थे। एक बार निकला ताम्रपत्र साल‑दर‑साल बिना भाला उठाए चुपचाप आज्ञापालन दिला सकता था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Halasi with temple, palace and inscription hall
panels.action: The town of Halasi spreads out with a modest palace, temples, and a hall where scribes sit with copper plates; Mayurasharma’s Land Grants stands outside, watching a young king figure receive counsel from a Brahmin advisor.

dialogue.text: By the time of Kakusthavarma, the Halasi plates look back and magnify Mayurasharma as the great giver—his brahmadeya policy turned into dynastic memory and model.

i18n.hi: ककुष्ठवर्मा के समय तक हलेसी के पट्ट मयूरशर्मा को और भी बड़ा दाता बनाकर याद करते हैं—उसकी ब्रह्मदेय नीति ही राजवंश की स्मृति और मिसाल बन गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of later rulers issuing similar grants
panels.action: A later Kadamba ruler, in slightly different dress, hands a copper plate to a group of Brahmins, echoing Mayurasharma’s gesture; Mayurasharma’s Land Grants appears faintly behind him like an echoing presence.

dialogue.text: The pattern spread. Later Kadamba kings continued grants to agraharas and temples across Talagunda, Banavasi, Halasi, Sirsi—a machine that could be copied, extended, inherited.

i18n.hi: ढाँचा फैल गया। बाद के कदंब राजाओं ने तलागुंडा, बनवासी, हलेसी, सिरसी भर में आग्रहारों और मंदिरों को दान जारी रखे—एक मशीन, जिसे नकल किया जा सकता था, फैलाया जा सकता था, विरासत में दिया जा सकता था।

panels.shot: soft focus shot of a present-day village with old inscription
panels.action: A present‑day Karnataka village lane, children playing and motorbikes parked, frames an old, weathered inscription stone standing near a shrine, while Mayurasharma’s Land Grants is barely visible as a transparent figure beside it.

dialogue.text: Later communities would tell origin tales, linking themselves to ancient grants and distant northern lands; the historian notes these as living memory, not as simple, literal descent.

i18n.hi: बाद की जातियाँ अपने आरंभ‑कथानक सुनाएँगी—अपने को प्राचीन दानपत्रों और दूर के उत्तरी प्रदेशों से जोड़ते हुए; इतिहासकार इन्हें ज़िंदा स्मृति मानते हैं, सीधे‑सादे रक्तवंश नहीं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on the etched words for ‘brahmadeya’ on a plate
panels.action: An extreme close-up shows the early script word for ‘brahmadeya’ etched into a copper plate, its grooves darkened with age, as the reflection of Mayurasharma’s Land Grants eyes shimmers on the metal surface.

dialogue.text: Upinder Singh and others see here a larger story: early medieval states turning to land grants, binding Brahmin lineages, shrines and agrarian surplus into the skeleton of power.

i18n.hi: उपिंदर सिंह और दूसरे यहाँ एक बड़ी कथा देखते हैं: शुरुआती मध्‍यकालीन राज्य, जो भूमि‑दानों से ब्राह्मण वंशों, तीर्थ‑स्थान और कृषि अधिशेष को सत्ता की हड्डी में बाँधते हैं।

panels.shot: wide, contemplative shot of Mayurasharma overlooking a patchwork of villages at dusk
panels.action: At dusk, Mayurasharma’s Land Grants stands on a hilltop, looking over a patchwork of lit villages, fields and temple spires; the forests beyond are dark, the sky deepening, as he rests his hand on a rolled copper plate.

dialogue.text: Mayurasharma’s true legacy lies not only in a warrior’s rise but in this agrahara village machine—a reminder that power endures when it settles into fields, teachers, stones and the daily rhythm of a land.

i18n.hi: मयूरशर्मा की असली विरासत सिर्फ योद्धा की उछाल नहीं, ये आग्रहारा‑गाँव मशीन है—याद दिलाती है कि सत्ता टिकती है, जब वह खेतों, गुरुओं, पत्थरों और धरती की रोज़मर्रा की धड़कन में बस जाती है।
